research_question: When a sender can choose both a costly signal and whether to submit to costly verification, does the availability of verification crowd out signaling or complement it?
conjecture: The availability of costly verification partially crowds out costly signaling: in equilibrium, high types signal less but verify more, and total separation costs decrease.
model_primitives: Two types of sender (high, low) and one receiver. The sender privately knows type. The sender chooses a signal level (continuous, costly) and whether to request verification (binary, costly to both parties). The receiver observes the signal and verification outcome (if requested) and sets a wage equal to the posterior expected type. Timing: sender chooses signal and verification simultaneously, then receiver updates and pays.
